newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Greenpeace says Cargill gets injunction against it.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace says Cargill gets injunction against it.

text.p: U.S. grain giant Cargill has taken out an injunction banning Greenpeace from interfering with the arrival this weekend of another load of genetically modified soybeans, the environment pressure group said on Friday.

Greenpeace said it faced fines of one million francs ($30,000) an hour if it comes within one kilometre of the grain ship Stanislaw Kulczynski which is due to arrive in the Belgian port of Antwerp over the weekend.
Greenpeace has launched a worldwide campaign against the spread of genetically modified foods which it says are untested and a potential environmental time-bomb.

Earlier this week the Greenpeace ship Sirius was impounded in Antwerp and faced with a fine of $19,000 for interfering with the arrival last week of the grain freighter Bunga Saga Empa, which was also carrying modified soybeans.

Shortly before that it had called off another action against a Cargill shipment when the world's biggest privately owned grain company took out an injunction that also carried with it fines of $30,000 an hour for any breach.
The European Union has no full policy on genetically changed food, although it has approved the importation of some specific modifications.
On Thursday the European Parliament urged EU governments to segregate and specifically label modified soybeans.
Greenpeace did not say if it intended to abide by the latest injunction or at any rate mount a protest when the Stanislaw Kulczynski arrives in Antwerp.
